examples.purpose: Bun now ships a built-in image processing API that handles JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, and BMP — plus HEIC, AVIF, and TIFF on macOS and Windows — with zero native module installs. Bun.Image provides a chainable pipeline for decoding, transforming
All processing runs off the main thread (except metadata()). Output via .bytes(), .buffer(), .blob(), .toBase64(), .dataurl(), .placeholder() (thumbhash), .metadata(), or .write(dest).
Bun.Image instances work directly as response/request bodies with automatic Content-Type:
examples.code: return new Response(new Bun.Image(upload).resize(200).jpeg());

examples.section: Recursive watching now tracks new directories (Linux)
examples.purpose: Previously, fs.watch("dir", { recursive: true }) only registered the directory tree that existed at the time watch() was called. Directories created after the watch started were never tracked, so files inside them were invisible to the watc

examples.section: --no-orphans — exit when the parent process dies
examples.purpose: Bun now supports an opt-in mode that automatically exits when its parent process dies — even if the parent was SIGKILLed and never had a chance to forward a signal. On exit, Bun also recursively SIGKILLs every descendant process it spawned.
examples.code:
# CLI flag (new)
bun --no-orphans run my-script

# bunfig.toml
[run]
noOrphans = true

# Environment variable
BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_NO_ORPHANS=1 bun run my-script

examples.purpose: Bun now implements process.execve(execPath, args, env), matching the API added in Node.js v24. This POSIX syscall replaces the current process image in-place — it never returns on success.
Bun.Terminal and Bun.spawn({ terminal }) now work on Windows, powered by the Windows ConPTY API (CreatePseudoConsole). Previously, Bun.Terminal was only available on macOS and Linux.

examples.section: Pipeline producer exit no longer clobbers downstream pager's terminal state
examples.purpose: When piping Bun's output to tools like less, fzf, or fx (e.g. bun script.js | less), Bun would unconditionally restore its startup terminal (termios) snapshot at exit. Because termios state belongs to the underlying /dev/pts/ device — not t
examples.code:
# Before: 'q' does nothing in less — terminal is stuck in cooked/line-buffered mode
bun app.js | less

# After: less, fzf, fx, and other pagers work correctly
bun app.js | less
